summary_md:
Revision 30 writes D289's two scope limits. R29, R53 and, through R29, P18: while the lock is off the MCP server hands out its ASGI apps behind a lock check that fails start-up, answers 503 and closes websockets once the lock is on; under the lock none is handed out; a socket an embedder's own server opens for a saved app before start-up is that server's doing, outside R29.
R2: the loader and `cma import monzo` read a file into memory, decode and split it, then read its records in one pass, one record ahead; reading as a stream is outside R2, and the previous release read no less.
82758a3 (T04) and 6b43212 (T17) already build both. verify-185 passed T04 on every criterion but R2; before its review T04 rewords two docstrings, a comment and a test name that claim nothing past the first problem is read.
Two questions: whether the ASGI app may be a wrapper of the SDK's app (default yes, as built), and when a lock turned on during a run takes effect (default: from the next run; T17 reads firm.yaml at a resume).
The design takes in verify-154 to verify-185, D259 to D286 and D289; Context, Options, C4, C7, C12, traceability, scope, Consequences, Interfaces, Failure modes, Migration and Consumer trace (item 31) change.

questions.context: What the MCP server's ASGI factories hand out while the lock is off (R53, D289; T17 at 6b43212). D289 says the server hands out its ASGI apps as the previous release did. 6b43212 hands out the SDK's app inside a lock check: a wrapper whose call reads the lock and whose every other attribute is the SDK app's (LockCheckedASGI, src/cma/mcp_server.py:82-107). Its class is not the SDK's, which verify-184 named as a minor change to the public return type. Revision 30's R53 says so (design default; no build change). The alternative hands out the SDK's own app, its class unchanged, with the lock check added to it as middleware that sees its start-up and every request, so an embedder's class check keeps working. That costs one change in T17 and its two tests that assert the wrapper's class (tests/test_firm.py:600 and :663).
options: The SDK's app behind a lock check, a wrapper, as 6b43212 builds; R53 says code that checks the app's class sees another class (design default; no build change)
The SDK's own app, its class unchanged, with the lock check added as middleware; R53 says so in the next revision (one change in T17 and two tests)

questions.context: When a lock turned on takes effect for a run already going (R29, P18; T17 at 6b43212, not yet reviewed). R29 is a state requirement: WHILE the lock is on, no hosted client is made and no network connection is opened. verify-182 and verify-184 each probed a reading of firm.yaml used after the lock changed. 6b43212 binds a reading to its run and firm folder (src/cma/firm.py:128-162), so the reading a run takes as it starts decides its hosted client, its hosted requests while it runs and its tracing. Two corners remain. A lock turned on during a run does not stop that run's later hosted requests, such as a redraft. A resume in a long-lived process judges 'on now' by the graph's latest reading where it has one (src/cma/graph.py:427), which can date from before the lock was turned on. The design default: a lock turned on takes effect from the next run, so a run's evidence never records a lock other than the one that governed it; a resume reads firm.yaml as it resumes; R29 and P18 say so in the next revision. That costs one line in T17. The alternative reads firm.yaml before every hosted request, so a run stops at its next request once the lock is on and writes no memo. That costs a file read per request and a run that can fail part-way with nothing recorded.
options: From the next run: a run keeps the lock its reading found as it started, and a resume reads firm.yaml as it resumes; say it in R29 and P18 in the next revision (design default; T17 changes the resume's read before its review)
At once: every hosted request reads firm.yaml as it is made, so a run stops at its next request once the lock is on and writes no memo (T17 changes its request check before its review)

proposals.text: T04, before re-verifying 82758a3 against revision 30: reword the docstrings of iter_data and _records (src/cma/ingest.py:281-282 and :338-339) and the comment at src/cma/importers/monzo.py:169-170 to say that nothing past the record a caller stops at is checked, since the whole file is read into memory and the next record may be read; rename test_monzo_reads_nothing_past_the_first_problem (tests/test_money_in.py:1482) to what it proves; claim only what the runner's tiers prove.

T17: re-verify 6b43212 against revision 30. The socket an embedder's server binds for a saved app before its start-up (verify-184) is outside R29. Under revision 30's default for a lock turned on during a run, make a resume read firm.yaml as it resumes rather than the graph's latest reading (src/cma/graph.py:427), with an invariants test named p18.

2026-11-21 When a requirement's guarantee depends on what another program does with what the package hands it (an embedder's ASGI server binding a saved app) or on bytes of a file after the one a refusal names, scope it at the first failed review rather than building another check: T17's ASGI major went round three reviews and T04's reader twenty-six.

requirements.md.new:
Revision 30, after D289 (changes requested on 2026-11-21, the owner's decision of 2026-11-20 given in chat, after T17's fifth review, verify-184, and T04's fifty-third, verify-185). R2, R29, R53 and P18 change; their ids, forms and risk tags do not. R29 and R53 met at the MCP server's ASGI apps, which an embedder's own ASGI server binds and serves. T17's first review, verify-122, failed R29 because an app saved while the lock was off could open its listening socket after the lock was turned on. The owner then refused every ASGI app, and verify-182 failed that against R53, since an embedder that mounted the app could no longer build it. The owner's next change hands an app out again while the lock is off, one that reads the lock at start-up and before every request, and verify-184 failed R29 again: an embedder's server with its lifespan events turned off binds its socket before anything in the app runs. Since revision 29, T04 was reviewed twenty-six more times, verify-154 to verify-185, and every review failed on R2. Each found one more way reading a statement or a Monzo export met a later part of the file before the first problem was named: a byte that is not UTF-8, a field too long to read, a quoted field left open, a row in another currency, and in verify-185 the whole export read, decoded and split into lines, and the next record read, before the first record was checked. D289 accepts these as outside the guarantee, to push development forward, and asks for two scope limits, which R29, R53 and R2 now state. R29 and R53: with the offline lock off, the MCP server hands out its ASGI apps (sse_app, streamable_http_app) as the previous release did. Such an app reads the lock at start-up and before every request and, once the lock is on, fails its start-up, answers every HTTP request with 503 and closes every websocket, so no request is served and nothing of the server runs; under the lock no app is handed out. A listening socket that an embedder's own ASGI server opens for a saved app with lifespan events turned off is that server's doing and outside R29, because refusing to hand out an app at all, the only way to keep such a server from binding, would break R53. R2: the statement loader and `cma import monzo` read the file into memory, decode it and split it into lines before reading its records; they then read the records one at a time, in one pass, and check each record once the next has been read, one record ahead, which is how a quoted field left open to the end of the file is told from a last record; and `cma import monzo` stops at the first problem it meets. Reading the file as a stream, and checking a record before the next one has been read, are outside R2. Revision 30 makes five readings. First, 'as the previous release did' is read as each factory handing out an app that an embedder can mount and serve with the same options, any attribute of which it reads as the previous release's app's: the app is the previous release's behind the lock check, not an instance of its class, and revision 30 asks the owner. Second, 'with lifespan events turned off' is read as one case of a socket the embedder's server opens or holds before the app has started up, as one does when it is handed a socket already bound, which is likewise that server's doing. Third, 'before every request' is read as before every request the app begins to serve: a request it began before the lock was turned on, such as a long-lived event stream, runs on, while a message a client sends after the lock is on arrives as a new request, answered with 503, and every MCP tool reads the lock when it is called and refuses before reading a file. Fourth, P18 asked that starting the MCP server under the lock fail before any network call is attempted, which an embedder's server that binds first never lets an app do; left so, P18 would ask for what R29 now puts outside, so it now says it through R29. Fifth, 'check each record once the next has been read' is read as at most one record ahead: a record that cannot be read whole (a field too long to read, a byte that is not UTF-8, a quoted field left open) is checked when it is met, and the Monzo importer checks no record after the one it stops on, though it has read the whole file and may have read the next record. Every other requirement, property, term and id is as revision 29 left it.

**What the owner decided on revision 29, and what T04's twenty-eighth to fifty-third reviews and T17's third to fifth reviews showed** (D259 to D286 and D289, verify-154 to verify-185, 2026-11-20 to 2026-11-21)
- D259 answered revision 29's question with its default: an output path another program, or a second `cma run` with the same --out, takes while the review waits is outside the export guarantee, as R53 writes it. D260 approved revision 29.
- T04 was reviewed twenty-six more times, verify-154 to verify-185, and every review failed on R2; the owner took the first twenty-five over (D261 to D284 and D286). In verify-185, at 82758a3, R1, R3, R7, P1, P2 and P6 passed. Each R2 major found one more way the reader met a later part of a file before it named the first problem:
  - *the order of a row's checks* (verify-154, verify-156, verify-161 to verify-163, verify-167): the Transaction ID, a surplus cell or the per-line limit was checked before the currency or the amount, a missing Date raised instead of being named, and surplus cells were ignored;
  - *a byte that is not UTF-8* (verify-156, verify-158 to verify-161, verify-165, verify-169, verify-170, verify-172, verify-173): decoding the whole export first let a later bad byte hide an earlier problem, and each way of reading on past one met one more corner: a file whose lines end in CR alone, a byte-order mark, a multiline header, a bad byte in a record's continuation line or in the first data record;
  - *a field too long to read, or a quoted field left open* (verify-160, verify-164 to verify-171, verify-173): the CSV reader read a whole record before its currency or amount was seen, recovery raised the process-wide field limit, a refusal said such a field would be past the limit, and a quoted field open at the end of the file was accepted;
  - *a row in another currency* (verify-174 to verify-177): skipped by its currency, its unreadable field still stopped the import, or a quoted field left open in it swallowed the rest of the export and the import succeeded, short;
  - *reading past the first problem* (verify-178, verify-180, verify-183, verify-185): recovery parsed the rest of the export, then rebuilt it for each oversized record, then read the body before the first row was checked.
  At 82758a3 the reader reads its records one at a time, in one pass (_records, src/cma/ingest.py:335-425). But the importer reads the whole export as bytes (src/cma/importers/monzo.py:154), decodes it (_decoded, src/cma/ingest.py:230-239) and splits it into lines (:252) before its first record, and holds each record (:352) until the CSV reader has read the next (:359). So a quoted field running over a very large number of lines after a bad first record is read before line 2 is refused (verify-185). The previous release read every record into memory before checking any (src/cma/ingest.py:63-67 and src/cma/importers/monzo.py:123-132 on the integration branch at b777195).
- Two R53 findings came in the same reviews and are answered. Staging names that could overwrite a sibling file (verify-154) are now a unique temporary name (src/cma/cli.py:339 at 82758a3). A lock taken by the checkpoint path as given, so that two paths to one file took two locks (verify-158), is now taken on the resolved path (:238).
- Minors recurred in every review: a scratchpad probe the runner did not run, historical test counts, and the committed example's evidence_note. Since verify-185, test_monzo_reads_nothing_past_the_first_problem (tests/test_money_in.py:1482) counts only the reader's requests for records, not the file's read, decoding or splitting.
- T17, the offline lock and what a prompt may carry (R29, R30, P5, P18), was reviewed three more times, verify-157, verify-182 and verify-184, and every review failed; R30 and P5 passed in verify-184. verify-157 found a run's lock taken from the caller's graph input and a custom rule id reaching the prompt. verify-182 found a bare boolean or a caller's configuration accepted as leave for a hosted request, and LangSmith tracing left on under the lock. Its R29 majors on the MCP server's ASGI apps went round once:

  - The owner then refused every ASGI app (478e616), and verify-182 failed that as breaking R53: an embedder that mounted server.sse_app() or server.streamable_http_app() could no longer build it.
  - The owner's c1bbe1a (D285) hands an app out again while the lock is off, behind a check that reads the lock at start-up and before every request and, once the lock is on, fails start-up, answers 503 and closes websockets (LockCheckedASGI, src/cma/mcp_server.py:82-107 at 6b43212); under the lock both factories refuse (:69-79). verify-184 failed R29 again: an embedder's own server with lifespan events turned off binds its socket before anything in the app runs, and a 503 afterwards cannot undo the bind.

- verify-184's other three majors are answered in 6b43212, the owner's fix for verify-184, not yet reviewed. A reading of firm.yaml decides only for its own run and firm folder: building one hosted client, and the run's hosted requests while the run is going (src/cma/firm.py:128-162). Each run's reading travels in its own config, not in a table by thread (src/cma/graph.py:415-431). A resumed run is untraced if the lock was on when it was drafted or is on now (:419-428). Tests at tests/test_firm.py:867, :892 and :912 mark them. Two corners stay, which revision 30 asks about (Options considered). A lock turned on during a run does not stop that run's later hosted requests, since its reading decides them while it runs. A resume in a long-lived process judges 'on now' by the graph's latest reading where it has one (src/cma/graph.py:427), which can date from before the lock was turned on.
- D289 accepts the two edges as outside the guarantee, to push development forward, and asks for two scope limits, keeping everything else in revision 29. Under R29 and R53: with the lock off, the MCP server hands out its ASGI apps as the previous release did; such an app reads the lock at start-up and before every request and, once the lock is on, fails its start-up, answers every HTTP request with 503 and closes every websocket; under the lock no app is handed out; a listening socket an embedder's own ASGI server opens for a saved app with lifespan events turned off is that server's doing and outside R29, since refusing to hand out an app at all would break R53. Under R2: the loader and `cma import monzo` read the file into memory, decode it and split it into lines before reading its records, then read the records one at a time, in one pass, checking each once the next has been read, and `cma import monzo` stops at its first problem; reading as a stream, and checking a record before the next is read, are outside R2. Revision 30 writes both.

- Still open at 82758a3: the docstrings of iter_data and _records (src/cma/ingest.py:281-282 and :338-339) and the comment at src/cma/importers/monzo.py:169-170 say that nothing past the record a caller stops at is read, which the build does not do and R2 no longer asks; T04 rewords them, and the test name, to say that nothing past it is checked, before its review. The Windows lock call still gives up after about ten seconds (src/cma/cli.py:248), which Rollout step 3's Windows run covers.
- Still open at 6b43212: verify-184's minors, a CLI exit status for a failed hosted request that no CLI test proves and a performance claim the runner does not measure.
- The lesson is revision 23's, at the edge of the package. A guarantee about what another program does with what the package hands it, or about how much of a file the reader touches before it names the first problem, cannot be kept by the package's checks, and each review found the next way round them. Stating where the package's reach ends, at the embedder's own server and at the file read whole, ends the search.

## Decision
design.md.new:
(b) costs one change in T04 and a file system with hard links, which the case store already needs. *Chose (a)*, the owner's answer (D259).

**Sub-decision: how much of a file is read before its first record is checked (revision 30, after verify-178 to verify-185; D289, in R2 since revision 30).** (i) Read the file as a stream: decode it as it is read and feed the CSV reader line by line from the file, so that a refusal reads nothing after the record it names but the reader's look at the next. A byte-order mark, a file whose lines end in CR alone, the decoder's and the CSV reader's own buffering and the test for a quoted field open to the end of the file would each need code of its own, and each review would test one more. (ii) Read the file into memory, decode it and split it into lines, then read its records in one pass, one record ahead (82758a3). (iii) As (ii), but check each record before the next is read: a record whose last field is a quoted field left open to the end of the file cannot then be told from a last record, since only the next read finds the end. *Chose (ii)*, the owner's answer (D289), which R2 says since revision 30. The previous release read every record into memory before checking any (src/cma/ingest.py:63-67 and src/cma/importers/monzo.py:123-132 on the integration branch), so (ii) reads no more than it did. What (ii) costs: a refusal of a file whose later part is very large comes only once that part has been read, decoded and split, and a file too large for memory is outside this release; a small business's statement export is far below either.

**Sub-decision: the MCP server's ASGI apps (revision 30, after verify-122, verify-182 and verify-184; D289, in R29, R53 and P18 since revision 30).** The SDK's server gives an embedder two factories, sse_app() and streamable_http_app(), whose apps the embedder's own ASGI server binds and serves. (i) Hand out no app at all, so nothing the package hands out can listen under the lock (478e616): verify-182 failed it, since every embedder that mounts the app stops working with the lock off as well as on, which R53 rules out. (ii) While the lock is off, hand the app out behind a check that reads the lock at start-up and before every request and, once the lock is on, fails start-up, answers 503 and closes websockets; under the lock refuse; and state that a socket an embedder's server opens for a saved app before the app starts up is that server's doing (c1bbe1a, 6b43212). (iii) Hand the app out and read the lock again when the server binds: ASGI gives an app no such moment, and a server that binds before start-up, or is handed a bound socket, never calls the app first. *Chose (ii)*, the owner's answer (D289). What (ii) costs: an embedder that saved an app while the lock was off and starts it under the lock in a server with lifespan events turned off opens a listening socket. Every request on it gets 503 and no tool runs, so nothing is read or sent, but the port stays open until the embedder stops it. A server that starts the app up before it binds, as uvicorn does with lifespan events on, stops without binding. *What the app handed out is:* (a) the SDK's app behind the lock check, a wrapper whose every attribute but its call is the SDK app's, as 6b43212 builds; code that checks the app's class sees another class (design default; R53 since revision 30). (b) The SDK's own app, its class unchanged, with the lock check added to it as middleware that sees its start-up and every request, before it is handed out. (a) costs no build change. (b) costs one change in T17 and its two tests that assert the wrapper's class (tests/test_firm.py:600 and :663), and keeps an embedder's class check working. verify-184 named the class change as a minor. Revision 30 asks the owner.

**Sub-decision: when a lock turned on takes effect for a run already going (revision 30, after verify-182 and verify-184; asked).** R29 is a state requirement: WHILE the lock is on, no hosted client is made and no network connection opened. verify-182 and verify-184 each probed a reading of firm.yaml used after the lock changed. 6b43212 binds a reading to its run and firm folder (Context), so the reading a run takes as it starts decides its hosted client, its hosted requests while it runs, and its tracing. (a) A lock turned on takes effect from the next run. A run keeps the lock its reading found, and its evidence records that lock truly. A resume reads firm.yaml as it resumes, and is under the lock if its draft was or if firm.yaml says so then. R29 and P18 say so in the next revision (design default; T17 makes the resume read firm.yaml rather than the graph's latest reading, src/cma/graph.py:427, before its review). (b) At once: every hosted request reads firm.yaml as it is made, so a run stops at its next request once the lock is on and writes no memo; tracing is still chosen as each invocation starts. (a) because a run is short and makes one draft, its evidence never records a lock other than the one that governed it, and a firm that turns the lock on mid-run gets the next run's refusal; it costs one line in T17. (b) closes the moment between a run's start and its last request, at the cost of a file read per request and a run that can fail part-way with nothing recorded. Revision 30 asks the owner.
